name: OpenCPN
summary: Cross-platform open-source chartplotter and navigation application that displays raster and S-57 vector charts, ingests GPS and AIS feeds, and runs waypoint routes. Large plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: The de facto open maritime nav display; a ready-made situational awareness front end for any surface-vessel or GNSS-denied maritime demo.
hackathon_notes: Install the packaged build, feed it NMEA over UDP/TCP from your own nav filter or a simulator and you have a chart display in minutes. Writing a plugin needs the plugin SDK and a full C++ build.

name: OpenCPN radar_pi
summary: OpenCPN plugin that connects to Navico and some Garmin and Raymarine marine radars and overlays radar imagery and ARPA-style targets on the chart.
why_it_matters: Shows how real marine radar returns are pulled into an open nav display, useful for radar-aided navigation and contact tracking demos.
hackathon_notes: Needs a supported radar on the network to be interesting; without hardware, study the protocol decoding and overlay code.

name: pyais
summary: Python library for decoding and encoding AIS NMEA sentences (AIVDM/AIVDO), including multi-part messages and streaming from sockets or files.
why_it_matters: The quickest path from raw AIS sentences to typed vessel positions for maritime picture building or AIS spoofing/anomaly detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyais, point it at a public AIS TCP feed or a recorded NMEA file, and you have vessel tracks in an hour. Pair with AIS-catcher for live RF.

name: noaadata
summary: Pure-Python AIS decode and encode library from a long-time AIS researcher, with message definitions and utilities for working with NOAA and coastal AIS data.
why_it_matters: A reference-quality alternative decoder, handy for cross-checking pyais output and for older message types.
hackathon_notes: Use mainly as a cross-check; pyais has the friendlier API.

name: AIS-catcher
summary: AIS receiver and decoder for cheap SDRs (RTL-SDR, Airspy, HackRF, SDRplay, SoapySDR) with a built-in web map, JSON/NMEA output and feed sharing.
why_it_matters: Turns a 30-dollar dongle into a live maritime picture sensor, the cheapest real RF input for a maritime awareness build.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binaries and Docker image; plug an RTL-SDR with a VHF antenna, run with the web viewer enabled, forward NMEA to pyais or OpenCPN. Inland sites may see few ships.

name: Signal K Server
summary: Node.js server implementing the Signal K open marine data standard: it ingests NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 and other boat buses and republishes everything as a JSON data model over REST and WebSocket, with a plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: A modern data bus for a vessel; ideal glue between sensors, your own nav filter and displays.
hackathon_notes: Run via Docker or npm, enable the sample data playback, subscribe over WebSocket. Write a plugin to inject an alternative position source.

name: Signal K Specification
summary: The JSON schema and specification for the Signal K marine data format covering navigation, environment, propulsion and other vessel data paths.
why_it_matters: Gives a common vocabulary for maritime nav data instead of inventing one during a hackathon.
hackathon_notes: Read the navigation.* paths before designing your own message format.

name: signalk-to-nmea0183
summary: Signal K server plugin that converts Signal K data back into NMEA 0183 sentences for legacy displays and autopilots.
why_it_matters: Lets a custom position or heading source reach any off-the-shelf NMEA consumer such as OpenCPN or a chartplotter.
hackathon_notes: Enable in the Signal K admin UI, choose sentences, output over TCP.

name: MOOS-IvP
summary: Long-running autonomy middleware (MOOS) plus the IvP Helm behaviour-based multi-objective decision engine, used widely for autonomous marine vehicles, including COLREGs-aware collision avoidance behaviours.
why_it_matters: The academic and navy-adjacent reference for marine vehicle autonomy; much published USV/UUV collision avoidance work is built on it.
hackathon_notes: Builds on Linux/macOS with CMake; the bundled alpha and heron missions run in simulation with pMarineViewer. Pair with the MIT 2.680 labs.

name: MOOS-IvP COLREGs master's research code
summary: MOOS-IvP applications from a 2025 master's project at Universidade de Sao Paulo implementing COLREGs-compliant collision avoidance for USVs, including a modified A* planner, a velocity-obstacle method and a virtual-contact spawner for test encounters.
why_it_matters: Recent, field-validated COLREGs avoidance code that plugs straight into MOOS-IvP.
hackathon_notes: Build against a MOOS-IvP tree; use pContactSpawn to stage head-on/crossing/overtaking cases. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default. The README says terms are 'specified in the repository' but none are.

name: NTNU colav-simulator
summary: Python framework from the NTNU Autoship centre for simulating and evaluating autonomous ship collision avoidance controllers, open-sourced in autumn 2025, with scenario generation and evaluation tooling.
why_it_matters: One of the few open, evaluation-oriented COLAV simulators from a leading autonomous ship lab; good test bench for COLREGs logic.
hackathon_notes: Python with uv; define scenarios and swap in your own planner. Pair with its VIMMJIPDA tracker for realistic target estimates.

name: VIMMJIPDA tracker interface
summary: Interface that runs the VIMMJIPDA multi-target tracker (visibility, interacting multiple models, JIPDA) inside the NTNU colav-simulator; open-sourced November 2025.
why_it_matters: A maritime-grade multi-target tracker connected to a collision avoidance loop, closing the sense-track-avoid chain.
hackathon_notes: Install with uv alongside colav-simulator; the VIMMJIPDA core tracker code is vendored in vimmjipda/code (also published on Code Ocean).

name: Aeolus Ocean
summary: Collision avoidance simulator for COLREG-compliant autonomous ship navigation intended for use as a digital twin under varied weather and day/night conditions. Distributed only as a Windows binary release (v1.11); the repo holds no source code.
why_it_matters: Another research testbed for COLREGs logic with environmental variation.
hackathon_notes: Binary only: download the v1.11 Windows release and run the .exe. Source is not published, so there are no build steps and nothing to modify or run on Linux. Little activity since 2023.

name: Virtual RobotX (VRX)
summary: Gazebo-based simulation environment for the RobotX maritime autonomy competition, with a WAM-V USV model, waves, wind, sensors and scored tasks such as station keeping, wayfinding and perception.
why_it_matters: The standard open USV simulator; lets a team test maritime nav and perception without a boat.
hackathon_notes: Docker or ROS 2 + Gazebo install; expect an hour or two of setup. Task worlds give ready-made scoring.

name: ArduPilot (ArduRover boat / ArduSub)
summary: Open autopilot suite whose Rover firmware has a boat frame for USVs and whose ArduSub firmware drives ROVs/AUVs, both with the EKF3 navigation filter and support for external position sources.
why_it_matters: The most deployable open USV/ROV autopilot; lets a team put a custom nav source onto a real vehicle via MAVLink.
hackathon_notes: Run SITL with the boat or sub frame; inject vision/DVL positions with VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE or GPS_INPUT MAVLink messages.

name: ardupilot_gazebo
summary: Gazebo Sim plugins that connect ArduPilot SITL to Gazebo physics, with example Iris copter and Zephyr plane models and worlds.
why_it_matters: Bridge for testing ArduPilot USV/rover nav in a 3D world.
hackathon_notes: Follow the ArduPilot wiki Gazebo guide; works best on Ubuntu (macOS also supported). No rover or boat models ship here, so a USV/rover test needs a model from elsewhere, such as ardupilot/SITL_Models.

name: MAVROS
summary: ROS gateway for MAVLink autopilots exposing state, setpoints and external pose inputs as ROS topics and services.
why_it_matters: Standard way to connect ROS nav stacks (DVL, SLAM, UWB) to ArduPilot boats and subs.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-mavros, then run install_geographiclib_datasets.sh; current MAVROS targets ROS 2 (Humble and newer). Feed your odometry into /mavros/vision_pose/pose.

name: BlueOS
summary: Blue Robotics' onboard software platform for ROVs and USVs: web UI, ArduPilot management, MAVLink routing and a Docker extension system on a Raspberry Pi companion computer.
why_it_matters: The default companion stack on BlueROV2 vehicles; DVL and USBL integrations ship as extensions.
hackathon_notes: Most useful with a BlueROV2; extensions are Docker images, so a nav add-on can be packaged quickly.

name: Water Linked DVL Python
summary: Example Python code for talking to Water Linked DVLs over their serial and TCP/JSON protocols, parsing velocity and dead-reckoning reports.
why_it_matters: DVL velocity is the core GNSS-free aid for underwater dead reckoning; this is the shortest route to real DVL data.
hackathon_notes: Archived by Water Linked and no longer maintained, but the serial (wldvl) and TCP parsers still work as examples. Needs a DVL or recorded JSON; protocol is simple JSON over TCP so a replay mock is easy. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: Water Linked DVL A50 ROS driver
summary: ROS 1 driver publishing Water Linked DVL A50 velocity and beam data as ROS messages; now archived.
why_it_matters: Reference ROS integration for DVL-aided navigation.
hackathon_notes: Archived; port the parsing to ROS 2 or use dvl-python directly (also archived). No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: Ping Python
summary: Python library and examples for Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 scanning sonar using the Ping protocol.
why_it_matters: Cheap altimeter and sonar input for underwater navigation and obstacle sensing.
hackathon_notes: pip install bluerobotics-ping; requires the hardware or Ping Viewer logs.

name: Ping Viewer
summary: Desktop application to view and record data from Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 sonar.
why_it_matters: Fast way to record sonar logs for offline SLAM or odometry experiments.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt releases; logs can be replayed into ping-python.

name: ping360_sonar ROS package
summary: ROS package that drives the Ping360 scanning sonar and publishes scans as images and laser-scan style messages.
why_it_matters: Gets low-cost scanning sonar into a ROS SLAM or obstacle pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Needs the sonar; the laser-scan output plugs into standard 2D SLAM tools.

name: Project DAVE
summary: Gazebo-based underwater simulation environment from the Naval Postgraduate School and partners, extending UUV Simulator with DVL, sonar, bathymetry and manipulation models.
why_it_matters: Navy-funded underwater sim with realistic DVL and sonar sensors for testing AUV nav without water.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 Noetic + Gazebo 11 via Docker; setup is heavy, budget half a day. No push here since 2024-08; the ROS 2 port continues in the IOES-Lab/dave fork.

name: NPS underwater multibeam sonar plugin
summary: GPU (CUDA) multibeam sonar simulation plugin for Gazebo producing physically motivated sonar imagery.
why_it_matters: Synthetic sonar data for testing sonar odometry and SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU; used within DAVE.

name: UUV Simulator
summary: Gazebo/ROS packages for underwater vehicle simulation with hydrodynamics, thrusters and sensors; archived.
why_it_matters: The ancestor of DAVE and many AUV research setups.
hackathon_notes: Archived; prefer DAVE, Stonefish or HoloOcean.

name: Stonefish
summary: C++ simulation library for marine robotics with hydrodynamics, underwater rendering and sensors including DVL, USBL, multibeam and forward-looking sonar; has a ROS wrapper.
why_it_matters: Actively maintained, lighter than Gazebo stacks, with acoustic nav sensors built in.
hackathon_notes: Build with CMake; use stonefish_ros for ROS integration. Good for a DVL+USBL EKF demo.

name: HoloOcean ROS bridge
summary: ROS bridge for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal Engine based underwater simulator with DVL, IMU, depth, sonar and acoustic modem sensors.
why_it_matters: Photo-realistic underwater sim with multi-agent acoustic comms, useful for cooperative AUV nav.
hackathon_notes: HoloOcean itself is not installed from PyPI (that package is an old 0.5.x): the source repo is only visible to a GitHub account linked to Epic Games, then pip install the client and run holoocean.install('Ocean') for the world package. The bridge is ROS 2 (Humble/Jazzy), Docker recommended. Needs a decent GPU.

name: USBL Simulator
summary: C++ library and ROS 2 (Humble) node that simulates ultra-short baseline acoustic positioning measurements; a Gazebo plugin is only listed as a planned feature.
why_it_matters: USBL is the main absolute fix for submerged vehicles; simulated USBL lets a team test an aided-INS filter.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 colcon build; generate USBL fixes to fuse with DVL dead reckoning.

name: AuvEstimator
summary: Work-in-progress AUV state estimator fusing DVL, IMU and barometer two ways, a 15-state EKF and a GTSAM factor graph with custom DVL and barometer factors, with ROS 1 (Kinetic/Melodic, Python 2.7) wrappers.
why_it_matters: Small, readable DVL-aided INS example to start a GNSS-free underwater nav filter from.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2021; treat as a starting template, not a dependency. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: SMARC navigation
summary: Localization and SLAM components for the SMARC AUVs (KTH), including EKF localization with IMU, DVL and multibeam sonar against a feature map.
why_it_matters: Research AUV navigation from a Swedish maritime robotics centre, showing map-aided underwater localization.
hackathon_notes: Fork of smarc-project/smarc_navigation frozen in 2021; the upstream was updated until 2024, so start there. ROS 1 era; read for architecture.

name: sonar-SLAM
summary: Underwater SLAM for robots with multibeam imaging sonar, from Stevens Institute research on BlueROV-class vehicles, combining sonar feature extraction and pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: One of the more complete open sonar SLAM pipelines; directly relevant to GNSS-free underwater navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 with sample bags; budget time for dependencies.

name: BRUCE
summary: BlueROV underwater SLAM and exploration code from Stevens Institute, combining sonar-based SLAM with active exploration planning.
why_it_matters: Predecessor to sonar-SLAM; shows SLAM-driven exploration underwater.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2020.

name: DISO
summary: Direct imaging sonar odometry: estimates vehicle motion directly from forward-looking imaging sonar frames without feature extraction.
why_it_matters: Sonar odometry is a key aid when DVL bottom-lock or vision fails in turbid water.
hackathon_notes: C++ with ROS; try on the provided datasets first.

name: Vortex AUV
summary: Guidance, navigation and control software from NTNU's student Vortex team for competition AUVs and ROVs, built on ROS 2.
why_it_matters: A complete, actively maintained student AUV GNC stack to borrow structure from.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 workspace; sim integration via their companion repos.

name: Autoware
summary: Meta-repository for Autoware, the open-source ROS 2 autonomous driving stack covering localization (NDT, EKF), perception, planning and control.
why_it_matters: The biggest open ground-vehicle autonomy stack; its localization modules are a mature map-based alternative when GNSS is degraded.
hackathon_notes: Heavy: use the Docker images and the planning simulator. For a hackathon, lift single packages such as NDT scan matcher or the EKF localizer.

name: Autoware Universe
summary: The broad package collection of Autoware with experimental and production-candidate modules, including localization add-ons such as YabLoc, landmark-based localizers and the pose estimator arbiter.
why_it_matters: Holds Autoware's extra localization modules; the core NDT scan matcher and EKF localizer have moved to autoware_core.
hackathon_notes: Pick packages and run them standalone with rosbags; autoware_ndt_scan_matcher and autoware_ekf_localizer now live in autoware_core, not here.

name: AWSIM
summary: Unity-based digital-twin simulator for Autoware with simulated lidar, camera, GNSS and IMU.
why_it_matters: Lets a team exercise Autoware localization without a car.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binaries for Ubuntu with an NVIDIA GPU. Licence is split: code Apache-2.0, but assets (including release content) are CC BY-NC, so non-commercial use only, and the docs may not be publicly re-hosted.

name: Baidu Apollo
summary: Baidu's open autonomous driving platform, including the multi-sensor fusion localization module combining GNSS RTK, IMU and lidar map matching.
why_it_matters: Its MSF localization design is a well-documented reference for GNSS/INS/lidar fusion in vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Very heavy to build; read the localization module docs and code rather than deploy.

name: grid_map
summary: C++ library and ROS integration for multi-layer 2.5D grid maps, widely used for elevation and traversability mapping.
why_it_matters: Standard data structure for terrain-aware off-road navigation.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-grid-map; convert DEMs or point clouds to layers quickly.

name: elevation_mapping
summary: Robot-centric elevation mapping for rough terrain navigation, started at ETH Zurich and now maintained by ANYbotics, that fuses range data into a probabilistic 2.5D map. This entry is the leggedrobotics fork of ANYbotics/elevation_mapping.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline for terrain mapping on legged and wheeled robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; this fork is dormant since 2022, while upstream ANYbotics/elevation_mapping was updated in 2024. Prefer the GPU version.

name: elevation_mapping_cupy
summary: GPU-accelerated elevation and traversability mapping from ETH Zurich, supporting semantic layers and learned traversability, used on ANYmal robots.
why_it_matters: Fast terrain and traversability maps for off-road platforms; current ETH practice.
hackathon_notes: Needs CUDA; Docker image available. Feed a depth camera or lidar and get a traversability layer.

name: traversability_estimation
summary: ETH package that computes traversability from elevation maps using slope, roughness and step-height filters.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable geometric traversability baseline.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, dormant; reimplement the filters with grid_map.

name: Wild Visual Navigation
summary: System that learns visual traversability online from pre-trained vision features and robot self-supervision, deployed on legged robots in forests.
why_it_matters: Learned traversability that adapts in minutes, relevant for unstructured off-road nav.
hackathon_notes: Needs a GPU and a camera bag; offline demo scripts help.

name: WayFAST
summary: Self-supervised traversability prediction for wheeled field robots that learns from RGB-D, with labels from kinodynamic traction estimates. The repo holds only the network models, one training notebook and a dataset download link; the traction estimator and navigation stack are not included.
why_it_matters: Agricultural/field traversability learning without hand labels.
hackathon_notes: Dormant; use for method reference. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: BenchNav
summary: Gymnasium-based PyTorch simulator for benchmarking off-road navigation planners under uncertain, probabilistic traversability, with synthetic terrain generation.
why_it_matters: Lightweight way to compare off-road planners without a robot.
hackathon_notes: Docker setup via make build-gpu or build-cpu, or pip install from the clone (not on PyPI); fetch the dataset and models with scripts/download_dataset_and_model.sh, then run the tutorial notebooks. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: RELLIS-3D
summary: Multi-modal off-road dataset from Texas A&M with lidar, camera, IMU and GNSS plus semantic annotations collected on a ground robot.
why_it_matters: A standard benchmark for off-road perception and localization.
hackathon_notes: Download only the sequences you need; ROS bags are large. Unmaintained since 2022; the data itself is static and still usable. Data and code are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, so non-commercial use only.

name: TartanDrive
summary: Tools and utilities for the TartanDrive off-road driving dataset from CMU's AirLab, recorded on an ATV with multi-modal sensors.
why_it_matters: Large-scale off-road vehicle dynamics and perception data for learning traversability.
hackathon_notes: Data is large; use the provided loaders and a subset.

name: HOUND
summary: Autonomy stack for a small-scale high-speed off-road vehicle from the UW MuSHR group, with BeamNG simulator integration and Jetson Orin deployment.
why_it_matters: Affordable off-road platform with sim-to-real tooling.
hackathon_notes: Docker-based install; real hardware optional. BeamNG license needed for sim.

name: FreeTAKServer
summary: Open-source Python server compatible with TAK clients (ATAK, WinTAK, iTAK) that relays Cursor-on-Target positions, chat and data packages.
why_it_matters: Gives dismounted users and robots a shared map picture; common endpoint for drone-detection and blue-force feeds.
hackathon_notes: pip or Docker install; point ATAK on a phone at it and push CoT from a script.

name: Crazyswarm2
summary: ROS 2 framework for flying many Crazyflie nano-quadrotors with motion capture or onboard localization, including simulation backends.
why_it_matters: The standard open stack for indoor drone-swarm experiments.
hackathon_notes: Simulation works without hardware; with Crazyflies plus Loco or Lighthouse you can fly a small swarm in a day.

name: Crazyflie firmware
summary: Firmware for the Crazyflie nano quadrotor including onboard state estimators and UWB Loco Positioning (TWR and TDoA) support.
why_it_matters: Readable embedded EKF with UWB ranging fusion, a compact study of radio-based positioning.
hackathon_notes: make and flash over Crazyradio; the kalman estimator source is a good reading target.

name: Loco Positioning node firmware
summary: Firmware for Bitcraze Loco Positioning UWB anchors and tags (DW1000), supporting two-way ranging and TDoA modes.
why_it_matters: Off-the-shelf UWB infrastructure for GNSS-denied indoor positioning tests.
hackathon_notes: Needs Loco nodes; configure anchors with the Crazyflie client.

name: cflib
summary: Python library for communicating with Crazyflies: parameters, logging, setpoints and swarm helpers.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to script a swarm or log UWB/estimator data.
hackathon_notes: pip install cflib; Swarm class runs parallel commands.

name: Crazyflie simulation
summary: Minimal simulation models and tooling for Crazyflie in Webots and Gazebo; the README says it is not actively maintained and not realistic in dynamics.
why_it_matters: Hardware-free swarm prototyping.
hackathon_notes: Webots is the easiest entry.

name: Aerostack2
summary: ROS 2 framework from UPM for autonomous multi-aerial-robot systems, with platform abstraction (PX4, Crazyflie, DJI, Gazebo), behaviours, state estimation and swarm mission coordination.
why_it_matters: Lets a team describe multi-drone missions above autopilot level and swap platforms.
hackathon_notes: apt install binaries; project_gazebo shows multi-drone missions in sim.

name: MRS UAV System
summary: Czech Technical University's multi-robot UAV platform with control, estimation (including GNSS-denied modes), planning and simulation, field-tested in outdoor swarm deployments.
why_it_matters: Mature outdoor-swarm stack with several localization back-ends to choose from.
hackathon_notes: Install via apt; simulation tutorials are good. Moving between ROS 1 and ROS 2 versions, so check the branch.

name: UVDAR
summary: Mutual relative localization for UAV swarms using blinking ultraviolet LEDs and UV-sensitive cameras, from CTU MRS.
why_it_matters: Radio-silent relative localization, attractive when RF is jammed or must stay off.
hackathon_notes: Needs special UV hardware for real use; simulated in the MRS Gazebo setup.

name: Buzz
summary: Domain-specific programming language for robot swarms with swarm-level primitives such as neighbour queries, virtual stigmergy and swarm membership.
why_it_matters: Expresses swarm behaviours compactly; used with ROS and drones in MIST Lab research.
hackathon_notes: Builds cleanly; bindings to real robots require extra work.

name: ROS2swarm
summary: ROS 2 package providing a library of swarm behaviours (aggregation, dispersion, flocking) and an easy-to-extend framework, tested on TurtleBot-class robots.
why_it_matters: Ready-made ground swarm behaviours in ROS 2.
hackathon_notes: Launch in Gazebo with multiple TurtleBots. Not maintained any more (README); branches target ROS 2 Dashing, Foxy and Galactic.

name: Swarm-SLAM
summary: Sparse, decentralized collaborative SLAM for multi-robot systems on ROS 2, supporting lidar, stereo and RGB-D with inter-robot loop closures under limited communication.
why_it_matters: Shared map and relative localization across a team without central infrastructure.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 with heavy deps; try on the provided datasets before robots.

name: DCL-SLAM
summary: Distributed collaborative lidar SLAM for robotic swarms with lightweight LiDAR-Iris descriptors for inter-robot place recognition and minimal data exchange.
why_it_matters: Low-bandwidth multi-robot lidar mapping.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 package; test with multi-robot bags.

name: CoLRIO
summary: Placeholder repo: it only holds a README pointing to zhongshp/Co-LRIO, where the code lives. CoLRIO is ROS 2 centralized lidar-ranging-inertial state estimation for robotic swarms that offloads optimization to a server and uses UWB inter-robot ranges (ICRA 2024).
why_it_matters: Shows how UWB ranging tightens swarm state estimation when GNSS is out.
hackathon_notes: Use zhongshp/Co-LRIO (Apache-2.0, C++). ROS 2 Foxy and GTSAM 4.2a8; build is sensitive to versions.

name: Kimera-Multi
summary: Index repo for MIT SPARK's distributed multi-robot metric-semantic SLAM system with robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: Strong reference for distributed visual SLAM under outlier loop closures.
hackathon_notes: Many sub-repos and ROS 1; better for study than a weekend build.

name: Omni-swarm
summary: Decentralized omnidirectional visual-inertial-UWB state estimation for aerial swarms from HKUST, combining VIO, UWB ranges and map-based place recognition.
why_it_matters: Shows fusing UWB ranging with VIO for drift-bounded relative swarm localization.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2022; superseded by D2SLAM.

name: D2SLAM
summary: Decentralized and distributed collaborative visual-inertial SLAM for aerial swarms from HKUST.
why_it_matters: Aerial swarm C-SLAM with distributed optimization.
hackathon_notes: Needs a CUDA GPU and the provided Docker images; runs on a quad fisheye rig, RealSense stereo or TUM datasets. Study rather than deploy.

name: EGO-Swarm
summary: Decentralized trajectory planner for single and multiple quadrotors in cluttered environments from ZJU FAST Lab.
why_it_matters: Popular lightweight swarm planning baseline with sim included.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 catkin build, runs in RViz sim within an hour.

name: uwb-localization (MAV swarm)
summary: ROS library fusing UWB ranging with IMU for accurate 3D localization of MAV swarms, used in a 2017 drone light show.
why_it_matters: Compact UWB+IMU fusion reference.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 and dormant since 2018.

name: Swarm relative localization (ETH PBL)
summary: Infrastructure-less relative localization for decentralized swarm formation of nano-drones using UWB ranging (IROS 2023).
why_it_matters: Relative positioning without anchors, the realistic case for field swarms.
hackathon_notes: The repo holds only a Python demo of the algorithm (demo.py) and a PDF supplement; no Crazyflie or UWB firmware is included.

name: UWB Software Library (USL)
summary: FreeRTOS UWB library for DW1000 on Crazyflie providing double-sided two-way ranging and UWB data messaging between drones.
why_it_matters: Peer-to-peer ranging building block for anchor-free relative localization.
hackathon_notes: Flash as Crazyflie app; ranging between two nodes in a few lines. Fork of iGNSS/uwb-software-library, tested against a pinned crazyflie-firmware commit. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: GEARdrones
summary: Lightweight STM32 drone control and multi-agent localization system combining a flight controller, UWB relative localization and a monitor tool.
why_it_matters: Low-cost hardware+software reference for UWB relative swarm localization.
hackathon_notes: Custom hardware; dormant since 2023.

name: UTIL UWB TDoA dataset tools
summary: Dataset and scripts for UWB time-difference-of-arrival measurements from Bitcraze's Loco Positioning System, collected by University of Toronto.
why_it_matters: Real UWB data for testing ranging-based estimators without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Download and run the provided EKF example as a baseline. Unmaintained since 2021; the data itself is static and still usable.

name: Stone Soup
summary: Open-source Python framework from UK Dstl and partners for developing, running and evaluating tracking and state estimation algorithms: Kalman variants, particle filters, JPDA, MHT, GM-PHD, track management and metrics.
why_it_matters: The most complete open multi-target tracking toolkit; the natural backbone for radar/RF/vision drone tracking and sensor fusion.
hackathon_notes: pip install stonesoup; adapt one of the tutorials (Kalman, JPDA, GM-PHD) to your detections. Built-in metrics make an honest evaluation slide.

name: pyMHT
summary: Track-oriented multi-hypothesis multi-target tracker in Python developed for maritime radar tracking research.
why_it_matters: Compact MHT implementation for comparison against Stone Soup.
hackathon_notes: Dormant; useful as a readable algorithm reference.

name: motpy
summary: Simple Python library for tracking-by-detection multi-object tracking with Kalman filters and IoU/feature association.
why_it_matters: Fast, minimal tracker to sit behind a drone detector in a demo.
hackathon_notes: pip install motpy; a few lines to track YOLO boxes.

name: BoxMOT
summary: Pluggable collection of modern multi-object trackers (ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, OC-SORT, StrongSORT and others) for detector outputs, in Python and C++.
why_it_matters: Drop-in visual tracking for camera-based drone detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install boxmot and wrap your detector; pick ByteTrack for speed.

name: ByteTrack
summary: ECCV 2022 multi-object tracker that associates both high- and low-confidence detections, improving tracking through occlusion.
why_it_matters: Strong baseline for tracking small, intermittently detected drones in video.
hackathon_notes: Use via BoxMOT or Ultralytics tracker configs rather than the original training code.

name: Ultralytics YOLO
summary: Widely used Python package for YOLO-family detection, segmentation and tracking with training, export to edge runtimes and built-in trackers.
why_it_matters: Fastest route to a custom vision drone detector trained on Anti-UAV or similar data.
hackathon_notes: pip install ultralytics; fine-tune on a drone dataset in hours with a GPU. Check AGPL licensing for deployment.

name: Anti-UAV
summary: Official repository of the Anti-UAV challenge and benchmark for detecting and tracking UAVs in RGB and thermal infrared video, with dataset links (Anti-UAV300/410/600) and baselines.
why_it_matters: The main public benchmark for vision-based C-UAS tracking, including thermal.
hackathon_notes: Download a subset, train a YOLO detector plus tracker, report on their metric.

name: UAV Detection and Tracking Benchmark
summary: Code and configs for benchmarking drone detection and tracking across Anti-UAV, Drone-vs-Bird and MAV-VID datasets, including format converters.
why_it_matters: Saves time on dataset wrangling for a vision C-UAS comparison.
hackathon_notes: Use the COCO conversion scripts first. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default. The three datasets keep their own terms.

name: Open Drone ID core C
summary: Reference C library for encoding and decoding ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN Remote ID messages carried over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Foundation for any Remote ID receiver; cooperative drone identification is the first layer of C-UAS awareness.
hackathon_notes: Compile and link into an ESP32 or Linux sniffer; includes test vectors.

name: Open Drone ID Android receiver
summary: Example Android app that receives and displays Remote ID broadcasts over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: A phone becomes a Remote ID sensor with zero hardware.
hackathon_notes: Build in Android Studio or use a store build; test with transmitter-linux on a laptop.

name: Open Drone ID Linux transmitter
summary: Example Linux transmitter for Remote ID over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Lets a team generate test Remote ID traffic without a drone.
hackathon_notes: Needs compatible Bluetooth/Wi-Fi chipsets; dormant since 2023.

name: Open Drone ID Wireshark dissector
summary: Lua Wireshark dissector that decodes Remote ID broadcast frames over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
why_it_matters: Debugging aid for Remote ID sniffers.
hackathon_notes: Drop the Lua into the Wireshark plugin folder.

name: RID (ESP32 Remote ID receiver)
summary: ESP32 Remote ID receiver built on opendroneid-core-c and a fork of sxjack's electronic ID classes.
why_it_matters: Ten-dollar Remote ID sensor node.
hackathon_notes: PlatformIO project for VS Code (not the Arduino IDE), developed on a TTGO ESP32 board with a 1.14-inch LCD; it shows lat/lon of one UAV on the display.

name: uav_electronic_ids
summary: Arduino classes for UAV electronic ID formats and ATM/UTM interfaces, including Remote ID transmit and receive on ESP32.
why_it_matters: Upstream of many hobbyist Remote ID boards.
hackathon_notes: Arduino IDE; the id_open examples are transmitters (ESP32, ESP8266, nRF52) and id_scanner is a receiver sketch.

name: DragonSync
summary: Gateway that converts WarDragon drone detections (Remote ID, DJI DroneID, ADS-B) into Cursor-on-Target for TAK/ATAK and optionally MQTT.
why_it_matters: Shows the end-to-end C-UAS chain from RF sniffers into a common operating picture.
hackathon_notes: Designed for the WarDragon kit but runs on Linux with ZMQ inputs; pair with FreeTAKServer.

name: WarDragon docs
summary: Documentation hub for WarDragon, an SDR-based RF sensing appliance for drone detection; open components are documented here, while commercial kits add closed features.
why_it_matters: Useful architecture reference for a low-cost RF C-UAS sensor.
hackathon_notes: Docs only; follow links to the open component repos.

name: WarDragon FPV energy scan
summary: GNU Radio based scanner that checks known analog FPV video frequencies for energy and publishes alerts over ZMQ; the optional confirmation detector is closed source.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable RF detection of FPV drones, a growing threat class.
hackathon_notes: Needs GNU Radio 3.10, gr-inspector and an SDR such as Pluto.

name: samples2djidroneid
summary: Decodes DJI DroneID (OcuSync 2.0) frames from SDR I/Q recordings, building on proto17's reverse engineering and Kismet.
why_it_matters: Recovers DJI drone and pilot location telemetry from RF, filling the gap for drones without standard Remote ID.
hackathon_notes: Needs high-rate I/Q captures; decoding is slow with interference.

name: dji_droneid
summary: Original reverse engineering of DJI DroneID with MATLAB/Octave scripts that demodulate frames, C++ turbo-code helpers and a GNU Radio correlation test flowgraph.
why_it_matters: Foundational work behind open DJI DroneID decoders.
hackathon_notes: Use for understanding the PHY; prefer samples2djidroneid for decoding.

name: DroneSecurity (NDSS 2023)
summary: Ruhr University Bochum receiver for DJI DroneID that works live with an SDR or offline on captures, released with their NDSS 2023 security analysis.
why_it_matters: Peer-reviewed DroneID decoder; authors note it is not being extended.
hackathon_notes: Run offline on the provided samples first; live mode needs UHD and a USRP.

name: RFUAV
summary: Code for the RFUAV benchmark dataset for UAV detection and identification from RF signals, using a two-stage STFT spectrogram detection and classification model.
why_it_matters: Recent learned RF drone classification with a public dataset.
hackathon_notes: Start from the provided spectrogram models; raw data size is large.

name: DroneRF
summary: LabVIEW programs to record RF signals plus MATLAB and Python code for drone detection and identification, accompanying the DroneRF dataset (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0).
why_it_matters: Widely cited RF detection baseline.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2021; good for a quick baseline classifier.

name: VolAnti
summary: Open-source acoustic drone detector that listens for propeller noise; explicitly detection and alerting only.
why_it_matters: Acoustic sensing covers drones that emit no RF, such as fibre-optic FPVs.
hackathon_notes: Breadboard build guide; new project, verify claims on your own recordings.

name: Batear
summary: Low-cost edge-only acoustic drone detector on ESP32-S3 with encrypted LoRa or Ethernet alerting.
why_it_matters: Cheap distributed acoustic sensor network for perimeter awareness.
hackathon_notes: ESP-IDF build; tune thresholds per site.
